subject: Edge surface latency spike — client runbook & immediate mitigations
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <ops@hybridworks.com>, Adam Lin <devops@hybridworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge surface latency spike — immediate note

Hi Priya / Adam,

Wanted to let you know we detected a transient spike in per-token latency affecting streaming responses routed through our us-west edge cluster between ~07:58-08:10 PDT this morning. Impact: intermittent slow token emission (200–800ms extra per token) for a subset (~3%) of connections which manifested as visible lag in your live-agent chat sessions.

What we did in the first 10 minutes: 
- Automated routing: flows hitting the affected edge shard were routed to a warm fallback pool (reduced CPU density) to keep sessions live.
- Prefix cache warm-up for longer-lived chats to reduce token re-computation.
- Applied a temporary runtime throttle to limit maximal in-flight tokens per connection.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations you can apply (low-effort):
1) Reduce client-side max_stream_tokens from 2048 -> 1024 for peak windows (reduces average emission latency).
2) If you use client-side retry on stream disconnects, add an exponential backoff (200ms -> 1s) and prefer reconnect+resume rather than full conversation rewind.
3) For agent UI: show a "Still working..." microindicator after 600ms to reduce perceived slowness.

I've attached a small telemetry snapshot and a step-by-step runbook for your ops team (mitigation-runbook-0909.pdf). We'll follow up with a post-incident note once we complete the root-cause analysis.

Apologies for the disruption — we're on it.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & post-incident runbook — Edge surface latency spike (9 Sep)

Hi Priya / Adam —

Thanks again for the quick changes on your side. We completed an initial investigation overnight and wanted to share findings and recommended next steps (short summary + concrete runbook). Full ticket: SERV-4821 (linked).

What we observed
- Window: 2026-09-09T07:58:10Z — 2026-09-09T08:09:50Z (us-west edge cluster).
- Symptom: transient per-token emission delay impacting ~3% of streams; median additional latency per token during window ~320ms, tail up to ~820ms.
- Root cause (prelim): a combination of a rapid kernel eviction cycle on a subset of edge nodes (evictions triggered by concurrent debug/telemetry jobs) plus a small regression in our continuous batching scheduler that momentarily increased head-of-line serialization. The evictions caused additional kernel compile/warm paths.

Actions we took
- Immediate: automated routing to warm fallback pool; prefix cache warmup; temporary throttle on in-flight tokens.
- Within 2 hours: disabled background telemetry snapshot jobs targeting edge kernels during peak hours; pinned the most commonly-used compiled kernels to reduce recompile churn.
- Within 12 hours: applied a scheduler fix (backported hotpatch) to reduce serialization for short-live streams; added a guard to prevent background jobs from evicting hot kernels.

Customer runbook (what HybridWorks ops can do now)
1) Client-side (fast): set client max_stream_tokens to 1000 during expected peak windows; enable reconnect+resume with exponential backoff as discussed (200ms initial).
2) Server-side (if you run a gateway): prefer streamed token batching at 16 token windows (reduces per-token overhead).
3) Observability: add this synthetic check to your monitoring (sample PromQL):
   sum(rate(redwood_streaming_token_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le) > 0.3 
   (alert when P75 increases > 200ms vs baseline).
4) Escalation: if you see >1% of streams with >500ms token tail for 10+ minutes, open an incident with priority and include the edge shard id.

Preventive roadmap items (what we will do)
- Harden kernel eviction policy and add a per-tenant hot-kernel pin list.
- Add a runtime knob to throttle background telemetry jobs when edge scheduler load exceeds threshold.
- Produce a short guidance note for customers on client config best-practices for large chat windows.

Attachments & links
- Attached: edge-telemetry-0909.png (time-series snapshot), mitigation-runbook-0909.pdf (step-by-step actions).
- Postmortem draft (internal link): https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/HybridWorks/0909-post-incident-notes

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min technical review with Karthik/Marissa this week to walk the runbook and answer engineering questions.

Appreciate your patience — we know these disruptions are impactful and are treating this as high priority.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
